question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

-513, -506, ? , -492, -485, -478, -471, -464
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. -499.

GIVEN

• -513, -506, ? , -492, -485, -478, -471, -464

SOLUTION

• The series increases by a constant +7 each step.

• -513 + 7 = -506; -506 + 7 = -499; -499 + 7 = -492 (matches next term).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the gap between two known terms: -485 to -492 is 7, so every step is +7. Add 7 to -506 → -499.

NOTE

• In an arithmetic (constant-difference) series, verify the common difference from any two consecutive given terms before filling the blank.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

? , 50, 148, 294, 880, 1758, 5272, 10542
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 26.

GIVEN

• ? , 50, 148, 294, 880, 1758, 5272, 10542

SOLUTION

• The operations alternate: ×2 − 2 and ×3 − 2.

• 50×3−2 = 148; 148×2−2 = 294; 294×3−2 = 880; 880×2−2 = 1758; 1758×3−2 = 5272; 5272×2−2 = 10542.

• The step before 50 must be ×2 − 2, so ? × 2 − 2 = 50 → ? = 52 ÷ 2 = 26.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Work backward: (50 + 2) ÷ 2 = 26.

NOTE

• When ratios between terms are roughly 2 and 3 alternately, test the pattern (×2−k)/(×3−k); confirm k from a known pair.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

O, V, C, J, Q, ?, E, L
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. X.

GIVEN

• O, V, C, J, Q, ?, E, L

SOLUTION

• Use positions (A=1 … Z=26) with +7 each step (wrap after 26):

• O(15) → V(22) → C(3, i.e. 29−26) → J(10) → Q(17) → X(24) → E(5, 31−26) → L(12).

• So ? = 17 + 7 = 24 = X.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Each letter jumps +7 cyclically; Q(17)+7 = 24 = X.

NOTE

• For letter series that wrap, add the gap and subtract 26 if the total exceeds 26.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

T, ?, Z, C, F, I, L, O
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. W.

GIVEN

• T, ?, Z, C, F, I, L, O

SOLUTION

• Use positions (A=1 … Z=26) with +3 each step (wrap after 26):

• T(20) → W(23) → Z(26) → C(3, 29−26) → F(6) → I(9) → L(12) → O(15).

• So ? = 20 + 3 = 23 = W.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Common gap is +3 (see F→I→L→O); T+3 = W.

NOTE

• Confirm the step from the clean run of later terms, then back-fill the blank.

question: If the month of November 2026 started on Friday, then which date will be the first Saturday of May 2027?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• 1 November 2026 = Friday. Find the first Saturday of May 2027.

SOLUTION

• Days from 1 Nov 2026 to 1 May 2027 = Nov 30 + Dec 31 + Jan 31 + Feb 28 + Mar 31 + Apr 30 = 181 days.

• 181 ÷ 7 = 25 remainder 6, so 1 May 2027 = Friday + 6 = Thursday.

• Thursday = 1 May, Friday = 2 May, Saturday = 3 May.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Odd days from Nov 1 to May 1 = 6; Friday + 6 = Thursday; next Saturday is the 3rd.

NOTE

• 2027 is not a leap year, so February has 28 days; count odd days (remainder mod 7) to shift the weekday.

question: A person was born on 21 September 2018. What day of the week will be on his 11th birthday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Friday.

GIVEN

• Date of birth = 21 September 2018. 11th birthday = 21 September 2029.

SOLUTION

• 21 September 2018 was a Friday.

• Over 11 years (2018→2029) odd days = 11 ordinary + 3 leap days (Feb 29 of 2020, 2024, 2028) = 14 odd days.

• 14 ÷ 7 = 0 remainder, so the weekday is unchanged → Friday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Each year adds 1 odd day, each Feb-29 in between adds 1 more: 11 + 3 = 14 ≡ 0 → same day.

NOTE

• A leap year contributes 2 odd days, an ordinary year 1; count leap Feb-29s that fall within the interval.

question: 5 girls A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Only E is to the left of D. Only C is to the right of A. Who is in the middle of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. B.

GIVEN

• 5 girls A–E in a row facing north; only E is left of D; only C is right of A.

SOLUTION

• "Only E is to the left of D" → D is 2nd from left, E is 1st: E, D at positions 1, 2.

• "Only C is to the right of A" → A is 2nd from right, C is last: A, C at positions 4, 5.

• Left→right: E, D, _, A, C → middle (position 3) = B.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• "Only one to the left/right" pins the two ends; the leftover letter takes the middle.

NOTE

• For north-facing rows, our left = position 1 (leftmost); read positions 1→5 from left to right.

question: 5 persons A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). C is at third position from right end of the row. A is fourth to the left of E. D is to the right of B. What is the position of D from the left end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Fourth.

GIVEN

• 5 persons A–E facing north; C is 3rd from right; A is 4th to the left of E; D is right of B.

SOLUTION

• C 3rd from right (of 5) = position 3.

• A four places left of E is only possible as A = 1, E = 5.

• Remaining positions 2 and 4 are for B and D; D is to the right of B → B = 2, D = 4.

• So order: A, B, C, D, E → D is 4th from the left.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• "4th to the left" needs a 5-gap span, forcing the two ends first; place the rest by the last clue.

NOTE

• Position from right = (n + 1) − position from left; here C: 5+1−3 = 3.

question: 7 boys A, B, C, D, X, Y and Z are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). B is not the immediate neighbour of X. C is fifth to the left of D. C is the immediate neighbour of B and Y. A is the immediate neighbour of Z and D. Who is sitting fourth to the left of B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. X.

GIVEN

• 7 boys around a circle facing centre; B not next to X; C 5th to left of D; C between B and Y; A between Z and D.

SOLUTION

• With 7 seats, "C is 5th to the left of D" = C is 2nd to the right of D.

• Fix clockwise seats: D, A, Z, X, Y, C, B (A between Z and D; C between Y and B; B's neighbours are C and D, so B is not next to X ✓).

• Fourth to the left of B lands on X.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• In a 7-seat circle, "5th to the left" = "2nd to the right" (7 − 5 = 2); build the ring from the neighbour clues.

NOTE

• Facing centre, left = clockwise; "k-th to the left" and "(n−k)-th to the right" are the same seat.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the box with top row P L M N and bottom row Q O R S.

GIVEN

• AEFG/HIJK : HAEF/IJKG. Apply the same rule to LMNS/PQOR.

SOLUTION

• Treat the 8 cells as a ring (top-left → top-right → bottom-right → bottom-left). Each letter shifts one place clockwise.

• Check: A E F G / H I J K → H A E F / I J K G (H moves up to front, G drops to the bottom-right) — a one-step clockwise rotation.

• Apply to L M N S / P Q O R: top becomes P L M N, bottom becomes Q O R S.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The bottom-left letter jumps to the top-left and everything rotates one cell clockwise; here P leads the top row.

NOTE

• In letter-box analogies, track each cell's movement (rotation/shift) rather than reading the letters as words.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first letter-number cluster in the same way as the fourth letter-number cluster is related to the third letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

AD120 : ? :: BK220 : DN720 :: DL170 : FO670
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. CG620.

GIVEN

• AD120 : ? :: BK220 : DN720 :: DL170 : FO670

SOLUTION

• Rule (from BK220→DN720 and DL170→FO670): 1st letter +2, 2nd letter +3, number +500.

• B→D, K→N, 220→720 ✓; D→F, L→O, 170→670 ✓.

• Apply to AD120: A+2 = C, D+3 = G, 120+500 = 620 → CG620.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters shift (+2, +3) and the number rises by a fixed 500; A→C, D→G, 120→620.

NOTE

• Solve the middle pairs first to extract the constant shifts, then map them onto the target cluster.

question:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Finger

2. Fine

3. Finite

4. Five

5. Firm
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 21354.

GIVEN

• 1. Finger  2. Fine  3. Finite  4. Five  5. Firm

SOLUTION

• All share "Fi". Compare 3rd letter: n (Fine, Finger, Finite) < r (Firm) < v (Five).

• Among "Fin-", 4th letter: Fine(e) < Finger(g) < Finite(i).

• Dictionary order: Fine(2), Finger(1), Finite(3), Firm(5), Five(4) → 2 1 3 5 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Sort by the first differing letter: Fine < Finger < Finite < Firm < Five.

NOTE

• A shorter word that is a prefix of another comes first (e.g. Fine before Finger).

question:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Epidemic

2. Epic

3. Episode

4. Episcopal

5. Epidermis
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 21543.

GIVEN

• 1. Epidemic  2. Epic  3. Episode  4. Episcopal  5. Epidermis

SOLUTION

• All share "Epi". Compare 4th letter: c (Epic) < d (Epidemic, Epidermis) < s (Episcopal, Episode).

• Epidemic vs Epidermis: "Epide" then m < r → Epidemic < Epidermis.

• Episcopal vs Episode: "Epis" then c < o → Episcopal < Episode.

• Order: Epic(2), Epidemic(1), Epidermis(5), Episcopal(4), Episode(3) → 2 1 5 4 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Epic < Epidemic < Epidermis < Episcopal < Episode (compare first differing letter).

NOTE

• Move letter by letter; the first position where words differ decides their order.

question:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Voltage

2. Voluble

3. Volt

4. Volley

5. Volume
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 43125.

GIVEN

• 1. Voltage  2. Voluble  3. Volt  4. Volley  5. Volume

SOLUTION

• All share "Vol". Compare 4th letter: l (Volley) < t (Volt, Voltage) < u (Voluble, Volume).

• Volt vs Voltage: "Volt" is a prefix of Voltage → Volt < Voltage.

• Voluble vs Volume: "Volu" then b < m → Voluble < Volume.

• Order: Volley(4), Volt(3), Voltage(1), Voluble(2), Volume(5) → 4 3 1 2 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Volley < Volt < Voltage < Voluble < Volume (first differing letter decides).

NOTE

• The shorter word "Volt" precedes "Voltage" because it is an exact prefix.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

276 : 506 :: ? : 483 :: 145 : 375
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 253.

GIVEN

• 276 : 506 :: ? : 483 :: 145 : 375

SOLUTION

• Rule: second = first + 230. Check 276 + 230 = 506 ✓ and 145 + 230 = 375 ✓.

• So ? + 230 = 483 → ? = 483 − 230 = 253.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The pair differs by a constant 230; subtract 230 from 483 → 253.

NOTE

• Find the constant additive/multiplicative link from the fully-given pairs, then invert it for the unknown.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

9 : 1331 :: 13 : 3375 :: 19 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 9261.

GIVEN

• 9 : 1331 :: 13 : 3375 :: 19 : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: result = (number + 2)³. Check 9 → 11³ = 1331 ✓; 13 → 15³ = 3375 ✓.

• So 19 → 21³ = 9261.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add 2 to the number and cube it: 19 + 2 = 21, 21³ = 9261.

NOTE

• Recognise perfect cubes (11³=1331, 15³=3375) to spot the "+2 then cube" pattern quickly.

question: In a certain code language, 'human react space' is coded as 'pa ps tq' and 'space has possibilities' is coded as 'tq tm pm'. How will 'space' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. tq.

GIVEN

• 'human react space' = 'pa ps tq'

• 'space has possibilities' = 'tq tm pm'

SOLUTION

• The common word in both sentences is space.

• The common code in 'pa ps tq' and 'tq tm pm' is tq.

• Therefore space = tq.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Match the shared word to the shared code; only 'space' and 'tq' appear in both.

NOTE

• In message-coding, the word and code common to two statements correspond to each other.

question: In a certain code language, 'RAGE' is coded '76' and 'POINT' is coded '60'. How will 'TAIL' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 65.

GIVEN

• RAGE = 76, POINT = 60. Find TAIL.

SOLUTION

• Take each letter's reverse-alphabet value (A=26 … Z=1), sum them, then subtract 1.

• RAGE: R(9)+A(26)+G(20)+E(22) = 77; 77 − 1 = 76 ✓.

• POINT: P(11)+O(12)+I(18)+N(13)+T(7) = 61; 61 − 1 = 60 ✓.

• TAIL: T(7)+A(26)+I(18)+L(15) = 66; 66 − 1 = 65.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse value of each letter = 27 − (its normal position); add them and subtract 1.

NOTE

• Reverse position pairs: A↔26, so value = 27 − normal position; useful for opposite-letter codes.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

ZUY8, WQT12, ?, QIJ27, NEE40.5
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. TMO18.

GIVEN

• ZUY8, WQT12, ?, QIJ27, NEE40.5

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: Z(26), W(23), T(20), Q(17), N(14) → −3 each.

• 2nd letters: U(21), Q(17), M(13), I(9), E(5) → −4 each.

• 3rd letters: Y(25), T(20), O(15), J(10), E(5) → −5 each.

• Numbers: 8, 12, 18, 27, 40.5 → ×1.5 each (8×1.5=12, 12×1.5=18, 18×1.5=27, 27×1.5=40.5).

• So the missing term = TMO18.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters drop by 3, 4, 5 per column; the number multiplies by 1.5 each step (12×1.5 = 18).

NOTE

• Handle each letter column and the number independently to spot separate arithmetic/geometric patterns.
